description: The figure contains two stacked line plots illustrating a sawtooth-like relationship between a vertical quantity and the horizontal variable \(m\), with a vertical dashed reference line at \(m_0\) in both plots. In both plots, the x-axis is labeled \(m\), uses a linear scale, starts at 0 at the origin, and extends rightward past \(m_0\); no regular numeric tick interval is shown beyond the labeled \(m_0\). In the top plot, the y-axis is labeled \(n\), uses a linear scale starting at 0, and includes dashed horizontal reference levels labeled \(w\), \(c-a-s\), and \(c-a\) (with \(c-a\) higher than \(c-a-s\)); the plotted line is black, solid, and unmarked, repeatedly rising linearly from near the level \(w\) up to near the level \(c-a\) and then dropping vertically back down near \(w\), forming successive sawtooth cycles that continue to the right of \(m_0\) with visibly smaller peak heights than the earlier cycles. In the bottom plot, the y-axis is labeled \(\mathrm{Size}_{\mathrm{run}}\), uses a linear scale starting at 0, and includes dashed horizontal reference levels labeled \(w+a+s\) and \(c\) (with \(c\) higher); the plotted line is black, solid, and unmarked, starting at 0 and increasing linearly up to approximately the level \(c\) before a vertical drop to a lower value, after which it continues as repeating sawtooth ramps and vertical drops across increasing \(m\), with the pattern persisting through and beyond the marked position \(m_0\).
